rawOutput.title: Personal Finance Fundamentals
rawOutput.topic: Budgeting, credit, debt, and index-fund investing
rawOutput.rationale: This is a practical mix of conceptual learning and problem solving. The sequence builds a cash-flow foundation, introduces interest before credit and debt decisions, then establishes investing concepts before an integrated financial plan. Guided examples come first because most areas are new, followed by retrieval and application. Sessions fit the three weekly availability windows. No knowledge-map topics were supplied, so topicIds remain empty.

sessions.title: Build a working budget
sessions.objective: Create a basic monthly budget from income, fixed costs, variable costs, and savings.
sessions.amountLabel: One monthly cash-flow model and one adjustment
contentTargets: Income, expenses, and monthly cash flow
Needs, wants, and planned savings
completionEvidence: Classify sample expenses as needs, wants, or savings
Construct a balanced monthly budget
Explain one adjustment for a budget deficit

sessions.title: Understand interest and borrowing costs
sessions.objective: Interpret simple and compound interest in everyday financial decisions.
sessions.amountLabel: Two interest models and two borrowing comparisons
contentTargets: Interest rate, principal, term, and compounding
APR and total borrowing cost
completionEvidence: Explain how rate and term affect borrowing cost
Solve a guided interest calculation
Compare two borrowing offers using total cost

sessions.title: Learn how credit works
sessions.objective: Connect credit reports, scores, utilization, and payment history to borrowing decisions.
sessions.amountLabel: One credit profile and one improvement decision
contentTargets: Credit reports and credit scores
Payment history and credit utilization
completionEvidence: Explain the difference between a credit report and score
Apply a utilization calculation to a sample balance
Classify actions by whether they generally help or harm credit

sessions.title: Choose a debt repayment approach
sessions.objective: Build a repayment order using balances, interest rates, minimums, and available cash.
sessions.amountLabel: One three-debt repayment plan with justification
contentTargets: Minimum payments and high-interest debt
Debt avalanche and debt snowball approaches
completionEvidence: Compare avalanche and snowball repayment orders
Construct a repayment order for three sample debts
Explain the tradeoff behind the selected order

sessions.title: Practice budgeting, credit, and debt decisions
sessions.objective: Retrieve and apply the first four sessions to a realistic household scenario.
sessions.amountLabel: One integrated household case covering budget, credit, and debt
contentTargets: Cash-flow diagnosis
Credit and debt tradeoffs
Repayment-plan revision
completionEvidence: Recall the main factors affecting borrowing cost and credit
Apply a budget adjustment to free repayment cash
Construct and justify a revised debt plan

sessions.title: Understand index-fund investing
sessions.objective: Explain how diversification, risk, return, and index funds fit together.
sessions.amountLabel: One index-fund mental model and one fund comparison
contentTargets: Stocks, bonds, risk, return, and diversification
Index funds, benchmarks, and fund fees
completionEvidence: Explain diversification without implying guaranteed gains
Compare an index fund with a concentrated investment
Apply an expense ratio comparison to two sample funds

sessions.title: Connect investing to goals and accounts
sessions.objective: Match a financial goal and time horizon to an appropriate investment decision process.
sessions.amountLabel: Two goal scenarios and one contribution plan
contentTargets: Time horizon, volatility, and emergency savings
Taxable and retirement account basics
Regular contributions and rebalancing basics
completionEvidence: Classify sample goals by time horizon
Compare a taxable account with a retirement account at a basic level
Construct a simple recurring contribution plan

sessions.title: Create an integrated personal finance roadmap
sessions.objective: Apply the full sequence to prioritize budgeting, credit, debt, reserves, and investing.
sessions.amountLabel: One prioritized financial roadmap with four justified actions
contentTargets: Priority setting across competing financial goals
Integrated budget, debt, and investing decisions
Personal action sequence
completionEvidence: Recall the core principles from each major module
Apply them to a mixed financial scenario
Construct a prioritized four-step roadmap
Explain the reasoning and tradeoffs behind each step

rawOutput.title: Personal Finance Fundamentals
rawOutput.topic: Budgeting, credit, debt, and index-fund investing
rawOutput.rationale: This mixed conceptual and problem-solving plan begins with practical foundations, then builds through credit, interest, debt, and investing in prerequisite order. Eight focused sessions fit the three weekly availability windows. New concepts receive guided teaching before later retrieval, calculations, comparisons, and an integrated financial plan. Basic budgeting is briefly checked rather than assumed mastered from self-report.

sessions.title: Module 1: Build a working budget
sessions.objective: Verify budgeting fundamentals and create a practical monthly cash-flow plan.
sessions.amountLabel: One monthly budget with a cash-flow check
contentTargets: Income, fixed expenses, variable expenses, and irregular expenses
A zero-based monthly budget with a small buffer
completionEvidence: Classify sample transactions into income and expense categories
Construct a monthly budget in which income covers planned spending, saving, and a buffer
Explain one adjustment for handling an unexpected expense

sessions.title: Module 1: Prioritize saving and cash reserves
sessions.objective: Use a budget to set a realistic savings target and emergency-fund milestone.
sessions.amountLabel: One savings target and emergency-fund plan
contentTargets: Savings rate and goal-based budgeting
Starter emergency funds and full emergency-fund targets
completionEvidence: Recall the core categories of a workable budget without prompts
Calculate a savings rate from a sample budget
Construct an emergency-fund target and monthly contribution plan

sessions.title: Module 2: Understand credit
sessions.objective: Build a practical model of credit reports, credit scores, and responsible credit use.
sessions.amountLabel: Credit report basics and five major score influences
contentTargets: The roles of credit reports and credit scores
Payment history, utilization, account age, credit mix, and new applications
completionEvidence: Compare a credit report with a credit score
Classify sample behaviors by their likely credit impact
Explain two responsible ways to use a credit card

sessions.title: Module 2: Apply credit decisions
sessions.objective: Evaluate credit-card choices and calculate the cost of carrying a balance.
sessions.amountLabel: Two credit scenarios with utilization and interest calculations
contentTargets: Credit utilization and statement payment choices
APR, periodic interest, fees, and grace periods
completionEvidence: Calculate utilization for a sample credit limit and balance
Solve an estimated monthly interest-cost problem from an APR
Apply credit principles to choose between two repayment options

sessions.title: Module 3: Understand interest and debt
sessions.objective: Explain how interest changes debt cost and distinguish productive from risky borrowing.
sessions.amountLabel: Three debt comparisons covering rates, terms, and total cost
contentTargets: Principal, interest rate, loan term, and total repayment
Simple versus compound interest intuition
Secured, unsecured, fixed-rate, and variable-rate debt
completionEvidence: Explain how rate and term affect total debt cost
Compare simple and compound growth in a small example
Classify sample debts by type and financial risk

sessions.title: Module 3: Build a debt payoff strategy
sessions.objective: Choose and justify a payoff order while preserving essential cash flow.
sessions.amountLabel: One payoff plan comparing avalanche and snowball orders
contentTargets: Debt avalanche and debt snowball strategies
Minimum payments, extra payments, and emergency reserves
completionEvidence: Compare avalanche and snowball payoff orders for sample debts
Construct a monthly payoff plan within a fixed cash-flow limit
Explain why the selected strategy fits the scenario

sessions.title: Module 4: Learn index-fund investing fundamentals
sessions.objective: Build a foundation for evaluating diversified, low-cost index funds.
sessions.amountLabel: Index-fund basics, diversification, risk, and fees
contentTargets: Stocks, bonds, funds, and market indexes
Diversification, volatility, time horizon, expense ratios, and tax-advantaged accounts
completionEvidence: Compare an individual stock with a broad-market index fund
Explain how diversification changes company-specific risk
Calculate the approximate annual fee on a sample fund balance

sessions.title: Module 4: Integrate a personal finance roadmap
sessions.objective: Apply budgeting, credit, debt, and investing principles to one coherent financial scenario.
sessions.amountLabel: One integrated plan with four justified priorities
contentTargets: Priority order among cash flow, emergency savings, costly debt, and investing
A diversified index-fund approach aligned with time horizon and risk
completionEvidence: Recall key budgeting, credit, debt, and investing principles
Construct a prioritized financial roadmap for a sample household
Explain the tradeoffs behind each priority
Apply the roadmap to identify one suitable next action
